In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: • The evaluation of the measurement algorithms and their applicability for routing purposes.
the development of algorithms to support dynamic routing.
the following issues: • The design of an algorithm that allows the estimation of the link utilisation based on short intervals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the measurement of the link load in short intervals is not suitable for the calculation of the routing.

the short-term measurement-based link load estimation algorithm with its inherent oscillations can be successfully applied to dynamic routing, if the oscillations are damped and the measurement interval is chosen to be sufficiently short.
the measurement of the current load of the links in a network and the estimation of future load values is a very difficult problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to show that it is indeed possible to use short interval-based link utilisation measurements to support dynamic routing.
the short interval-based measurement is the only possibility to achieve a good quality of service for connectionless packet switching in a dynamic routing environment.
the short interval-based measurement and the estimation algorithms are able to provide a good estimation of the link utilisation and therefore of the link load.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a short interval for measuring the load of a link is a reasonable choice.
, in order to make the best use of a network’s resources and to provide the best possible quality of service to the users, the link load calculation must be based on the shortest intervals possible.
the performance of a routing algorithm is highly dependent on the measurement algorithm used to estimate the current link load.
